To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absorption of electromagnetic energy by biological tissue is strongly dependent on the frequency, polarization, and size of the tissue.

the absorption of radio-frequency energy by a whole animal is strongly dependent on the polarization of the incident field, and that the absorption is also strongly dependent on the size of the animal.

(a) the power deposition in the animal is a function of its weight; (b) the absorption is a function of the orientation of the body with respect to the direction of the electric field; (c) the absorption is not a function of the frequency of the applied electric field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a technique for measuring the absorption of radiofrequency energy by whole animals in a manner analogous to that for measuring the dielectric properties of biological materials.
the development of a new technique to measure the radio frequency absorption of animals and biological materials.
the effects of radio frequency (RF) radiation upon the biological system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a biological body depends upon its size, shape, and orientation, as well as on the frequency of irradiation and the polarization of the incident electromagnetic field.
the polarization and frequency dependencies of whole animal absorption are strong.
the absorption of electromagnetic radiation in biological tissue is a complex function of frequency and polarization of the incident radiation and of the size and shape of the tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the whole animal absorption of radiofrequency radiation depends strongly on polarization and frequency of the energy.
the absorption of radio-frequency energy in the whole animal is highly dependent upon the polarization and the frequency of the incident wave.

the whole animal absorption is highly sensitive to polarization and frequency of radio-frequency energy, and that the whole animal behavior is not a simple superposition of the behavior of its constituent parts, i.e., the tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the orientation of the animal relative to the electric field is the most important determinant of whole animal absorption.
the polarization and orientation of the animal with respect to the incident field must be taken into consideration when determining whole animal absorption characteristics.
the orientation of an animal or biological tissue in a radio-frequency electric field can be a significant determinant of the power absorption in the body.
